newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore RSS1 rubber down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore RSS1 rubber down on long liquidation.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market saw modest long liquidation for RSS1 grade rubber on Wednesday with the trade pondering how long rubber producers can hold off on sales with prices coming under pressure, dealers said.
"I understand there were some people who liquidated their positions by rolling their positions forward," a dealer said. "There was liquidation in RSS1 rubber."

Traders speculated as to how long rubber producers could maintain their offer prices with output from major producers rising sharply. "I don't think the producers can hold onto their prices," one dealer said.
Singapore rubber traders said they have also received reports that Thai producers have recently delivered a large amount of material in the southern half of the country.

News that Thai traders and rubber officials dismissed talk that China would buy up to 80,000 tonnes of RSS3 rubber for second half 1997 delivery was shrugged off by the market. The report had earlier triggered speculative play for RSS3 here.
"The talk on that has died down," one dealer said.
At 0945 GMT, July RSS1 was seen at 166.25 Singapore cents (US$1.16) a kg from 167.25 cents.
